newsitem.title: ITALY: Ex-Nazi calls Italian massacre "personal tragedy".
newsitem.headline: Ex-Nazi calls Italian massacre "personal tragedy".

text.p: Former Nazi SS captain Erich Priebke told a military court on Tuesday he considered his role in Italy's worst World War Two massacre a personal tragedy, but said refusing to take part would have changed nothing.

Priebke, dressed in a white shirt and grey jacket, read a prepared statement in Rome's high-security Rebibbia jail where he is standing trial on charges of complicity in the 1944 Ardeatine Caves massacre of 335 men and boys, 75 of them Jews.
"I had never killed before that day and, luckily, I have never had to do so again," Priebke said, speaking in Italian. He has previously admitted to killing two people in the massacre.
"As I have said many times, carrying out that terrible order was for me a horrendous thing, a personal tragedy.

"I believed, as I still do, that if I could have avoided that horrendous event, I would have done so but I knew like everybody that disobeying orders, my death and the persecution of my relatives would not have saved those men."
Priebke spoke for half an hour during his first appearance in the military court since the trial opened in April.
After the hearing, the 83-year-old German returned immediately to the Roman Catholic monastery south of Rome where he is under house arrest.
Priebke, who is accused together with former SS major Karl Hass with complicity in the massacre, was extradited from Argentina in November 1995.

He is being re-tried after a court last August found him guilty but ordered he be set free under a statute of limitation. The verdict, which sparked a storm of protest, was quashed on appeal before the retrial began in April this year.
Hass, who was originally a prosecution witness in Priebke's first trial, admitted while testifying that he had also killed people during the massacre.
Under Italian law, defendants are not obliged to attend trial sessions and the 84-year-old Hass, whose lawyers say he is unwell, has not appeared at any of the hearings.
The next hearing, on June 26, will be given over to a summing up by military prosecutor Antonino Intelisano. Civil plaintiffs will then present their concluding remarks.
